New England Patriots.thesis: A.J. Brown added to a 14-win AFC champion; PFF enters 2026 with New England as its No. 1 secondary. Strong prior, but Super Bowl-loss regression risk remains.

Buffalo Bills.thesis: Josh Allen remains Tier-1 QB. 2025 offense stayed strong; defense was the weaker side of the SRS profile.

Miami Dolphins.thesis: Major quarterback/secondary uncertainty keeps the prior below market-neutral. PFF ranks the secondary at the bottom entering 2026.

New York Jets.thesis: Large rebuild off a 3-14 season. 2025 defense collapsed after major trades; modest reset bump but high uncertainty.

Pittsburgh Steelers.thesis: Defense reinforced and PFF ranks the defensive front among the league elite. Veteran-QB transition adds offensive variance.

Baltimore Ravens.thesis: Lamar Jackson plus Trey Hendrickson raises ceiling materially from an 8-9 season; still carrying prior uncertainty after 2025 underperformance.

Cincinnati Bengals.thesis: Healthy elite-QB ceiling supports an offensive rebound; 2025 defense was a major drag and remains the principal invalidation risk.

Cleveland Browns.thesis: New coaching regime, Myles Garrett departed, and the offensive line was rebuilt after a very poor 2025 pass-blocking season. High transition risk.

Jacksonville Jaguars.thesis: 13-4 in 2025 with a strong SRS and an eight-game finish; continuity around Trevor Lawrence makes this one of the more stable AFC priors.

Houston Texans.thesis: 12-5 with an elite 2025 defense; PFF enters 2026 with Houston near the top of both defensive-line and secondary rankings.

Indianapolis Colts.thesis: 2025 efficiency was better than the record, but quarterback health/continuity creates a wide Week 1 fair range.

Tennessee Titans.thesis: Low 2025 baseline, but a meaningful offseason reset creates some rebound allowance. Still one of the least certain priors.

Denver Broncos.thesis: 14-3, Bo Nix healthy, and PFF ranks Denver No. 1 on the offensive line. Jonathon Cooper availability is a defensive watch item.

Los Angeles Chargers.thesis: 11-6 despite severe OL disruption in 2025; healthy Rashawn Slater/Joe Alt combination materially improves the offensive prior.

Kansas City Chiefs.thesis: 2025 record lagged underlying defensive strength. Mahomes remains Tier-1, but return-from-ACL context makes early-season QB mobility a live variable.

Las Vegas Raiders.thesis: Large rebuild with Kirk Cousins and No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza in the QB room. Upgraded from a very low 2025 base but still highly volatile.

Philadelphia Eagles.thesis: Elite offensive line and strong defense provide a high floor. Coordinator/skill-position changes create more offensive uncertainty than the raw 2025 record suggests.

Dallas Cowboys.thesis: 2025 offense remained productive, while defense drove the negative SRS. Defensive personnel reset creates upside but large variance.

Washington Commanders.thesis: 5-12 baseline plus Laremy Tunsil torn triceps is a major Week 1 downgrade; PFF also has the secondary near the bottom entering 2026.

New York Giants.thesis: Low 2025 baseline but some offensive competence underneath the record. Offensive-line consistency remains a primary risk.

Chicago Bears.thesis: 11-6 division winner with a positive offensive profile. Defensive injury accumulation makes the Week 1 prior wider than the record suggests.

Green Bay Packers.thesis: Micah Parsons expected out early and Josh Jacobs is on the Commissioner’s Exempt List; both are explicit early-season downgrades.

Minnesota Vikings.thesis: 2025 defense carried the profile. New quarterback context creates offensive variance but home-field/defensive floor remain meaningful.

Detroit Lions.thesis: Elite 2025 offense, but both starting safeties and center Cade Mays are unavailable early; the Week 1 downgrade is concentrated on defense/continuity.

Carolina Panthers.thesis: Both starting tackles expected out initially and edge Nic Scourton lost for the season; significant Week 1 trench downgrade.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers.thesis: PFF ranks Tampa Bay’s offensive line No. 3 entering 2026. 2025 record understated some offensive stability.

Atlanta Falcons.thesis: Jalon Walker ACL and James Pearce Jr. suspension leave PFF’s preseason defensive-line ranking at No. 32; quarterback uncertainty remains.

New Orleans Saints.thesis: Low 2025 offensive baseline, but modest second-year/new-cycle rebound allowance. Rookie WR Jordyn Tyson absence reduces explosive ceiling.

Seattle Seahawks.thesis: Defending Super Bowl champion with the league’s best 2025 SRS. Strongest initial prior; regression and opponent offseason upgrades remain checks.

Los Angeles Rams.thesis: Matthew Stafford enters off an MVP season; Rams added Myles Garrett to an already elite front. Melbourne neutral-site travel increases Week 1 variance.

San Francisco 49ers.thesis: 12-5 2025 baseline and Mike Evans addition support offense; Australia travel plus Kittle/Bosa availability questions widen Week 1 uncertainty.

Arizona Cardinals.thesis: New Mike LaFleur regime and post-Kyler transition. Small reset bump only; quarterback and offensive-line uncertainty remain substantial.
